cases.description: a fresh burst gets no separator
a burst continuing a recent one is separated by a single space
no space before closing punctuation — otherwise you get 'word .'
same for a comma
same for a question mark
same for ) ] }
same for the ellipsis character
same for a percent sign
an opening delimiter still wants a leading space — deliberate asymmetry with closing punctuation
a new clause starting with ( wants its space
an empty burst after a recent injection
an empty burst with no recent injection

the separator is added blind, so text that already begins with a space would be double-spaced. Unreachable in the real pipeline (clean_text strips leading whitespace first) — pinned so a port that calls the units in a different order knows the ordering matters
RTL continuation still gets its separator
a burst opening with the Persian comma U+060C hugs the previous burst exactly like an ASCII comma — the pre-7.0.0 contract leaked a stray visible space here
U+061F suppresses the separator like its ASCII cousin
U+061B suppresses the separator like its ASCII cousin
U+00BB closes; it suppresses like ) ] } while U+00AB still counts as an opening delimiter

the probe skips invisible format characters, but a leading ZWNJ in front of a word still gets the separator: joining across a boundary ZWNJ is a normalisation decision (postprocess.persian_text strips boundary ZWNJ), not a spacing one
an RLE embedding character before a word behaves like the ZWNJ case: invisible, so it neither suppresses nor hides the separator — adversarial input must not make a port invent a special case
the probe looks past the leading ZWNJ and finds the Persian comma: suppression still applies even though text[0] is invisible — the pre-7.0.0 probe saw only text[0] and leaked the space
an RLE control before an ASCII comma: the first visible character decides, so the separator is suppressed
